SPECIFICATION FOR RUBBER GASKETS

1. Scope - Prescribes requirements and tests for vulcanized rubber gaskets of four different types for Each type is divided into a number of classes in different hardness ranges. various applications. 2. Typesand Classes upon the service conditions

2.1 Types-Vulcanized rubber gaskets shall be of four types depending and applications, namely: Type IGeneral purpose gaskets having superior General purpose gaskets having Oil resistant gaskets suitable gaskets. physical

0.1 This type refers to gaskets having superior physical properties, and useful at temperatures up to Either natural or synthetic rubber or a blend thereof shall be 7O"C, not resistant to oils or solvents. used in the manufacture of these gaskets Use of reclaimed rubber or ground vulcanized rubber is not permitted. 4.2 The gaskets are classified as given in Table 1. in five classes ( A, B, C, D and E ) and their physical properties shall be

If the gaskets are to be used for food products, the water shall be free from turbidity, odour or taste at the end of the test. 5. Specific Requirements for Type II

5.1 This type refers to gaskets having moderately good physical properties and not intended for use in stringent working conditions. Either natural or synthetic rubber or a blend thereof may be used in their manufacture. Reclaimed rubber and ground vulcanized rubber may also be used.

Specific Requirements for Type III Oil Resistant Gaskets

6.1 The gaskets of this type shall be suitable for hydro-carbon oils and fuels having aromatic content not exceeding 25 percent. For gaskets for use in oils having higher aromatic content, the manufacturer may be consulted. 8. Test

Methods in

6.1 Hardness - Hardness of the gaskets shall be tested in accordance with the method prescribed IS : 3400 ( Part 2 )-1980 `Methods of test for vulcanized rubbers: Part 2 Hardness (first revision )`.

with method 8.2 Tensile Strength and Ultimate Elongation - Shall be carried out in accordance prescribed in IS : 3400 ( Part 1 )-1977 `Methods of test for vulcanized rubbers: Part 1 Tensile stress-strain properties ( first revision )' using type I dumbell test piece. 6.3 Accelerated Ageing - The test pieces shall be subjected to this test in accordance with method prescribed in IS : 3400 ( Part 4 )-1978 `Methods of test for vulcanized rubbers: Part 4 Accelerated ageing ( firsf revision )`. 8.4 Compression Set - Compression set shall be tested at 70 f 1�C for 24 hours under 25 percent strain according to the method prescribed in IS : 3400 ( Part lo)-1977 `Methods of tests for vulcanized rubbers: Part 10 Compression set at constant strain'. Recovery time of 60 minutes shall be allowed. 8.5 For all types of gaskets, two test slabs, each of the following a) 150 x 150 x 2.5 mm, and b) 150 x 150 x 10 mm. 3 sizes shall be supplied:

IS : 11149 - 1984
8.5.1These slabs shall be compounded identically and cured to the same degree as the gaskets. all tests shall be carried out

8.8 Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, within 3 months from the receipt of the material by the purchaser.

a. Sampling - Unless otherwise agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, the procedure given in IS : 2500 ( Parts 1 and 2) `Sampling inspection tables: Part 1 Inspection by attributes and by count of defects, Part 2 Inspection by variables for percent defectives' shall be followed.

APPENDIX ( Clause
RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING 11 )

B

STORAGE

AFTER

RECEIPT

B-l. To maintain the gasket in optimum condition they should be stored in cool and dark place. If there is any doubt about the condition of gasket, they should be retested before putting into service. B-2. Products should be issued in the order of their date of manufacture.
